bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42485152 (haproxy): Heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 1 found by fuzz target fuzz_cfg_parser [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42485152
bug_description.normalized: In readcfgfile(), after fgets reads a line into a heap-allocated buffer, the code computes the string end pointer via end = line + strlen(line). When the input begins with a NUL byte (0x00), strlen returns 0, yielding end == line. The code then unconditionally executes *(end - 1) = 0 to strip a trailing newline, but with end == line this dereferences line - 1, which is 1 byte before the heap-allocated buffer. This causes a 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow WRITE to the left of the allocation. The fix adds a guard end > line before the dereference.

source.code: while (fgets(thisline + readbytes, linesize - readbytes, f) != NULL)
source.description: fgets reads attacker-controlled data from the PoC file into the heap-allocated buffer thisline. The PoC data begins with a NUL byte (0x00), so the buffer's first byte is '\0'.
source.value_from: Attacker-controlled file content written by the fuzzer harness; the PoC is 50 bytes starting with a NUL byte (0x00).

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: Writes a NUL byte at end - 1. With end == line == thisline, this writes to thisline - 1, which is 1 byte before the start of the 2048-byte heap allocation. ASan detects heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1 at 1 byte to the left of the allocated region.

root_cause.description: The code unconditionally dereferences *(end - 1) without first checking that end > line. When end == line (because the string is empty due to a leading NUL byte), end - 1 points before the heap buffer. The fix adds the guard end > line before the dereference.

tainted_value_origin.code: while (fgets(thisline + readbytes, linesize - readbytes, f) != NULL)
tainted_value_origin.description: fgets reads attacker-controlled file content into the thisline buffer. The first byte is 0x00, causing strlen to return 0 and end to equal line.

fine_trace.note: Allocates a 2048-byte heap buffer (linesize == LINESIZE == 2048). The valid write range is [thisline, thisline + 2048). Any access to thisline - 1 is out of bounds.

fine_trace.code: while (fgets(thisline + readbytes, linesize - readbytes, f) != NULL)
fine_trace.note: Reads attacker-controlled file content into thisline (readbytes == 0). The PoC's first byte is 0x00; fgets stores it at thisline[0] and continues reading the remaining 49 bytes. The NUL byte at position 0 will cause strlen to report an empty string.

Computes the end-of-string pointer. line aliases thisline (assigned at line 1873). Since thisline[0] == '\0', strlen(line) returns 0, so end == line == thisline. This zero-length result is the vulnerability-relevant derivation: end is not beyond line.

Writes NUL to end - 1 to strip a trailing newline. Missing guard: end > line is not checked. With end == line == thisline, end - 1 == thisline - 1, which is 1 byte before the 2048-byte heap allocation. ASan detects heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1 at address 1 byte to the left of the region allocated at line 1858. The fix adds the condition end > line before this dereference.

parser_admitted.description: The PoC file is at least 50 bytes (the fuzzer minimum). fgets successfully reads data into thisline and returns non-NULL, entering the while-loop body. The line-too-long realloc branch at line 1884 is not taken because end - line (0) != linesize - 1 (2047). Execution falls through directly to the vulnerable *(end - 1) = 0 at line 1909.

format.name: raw
format.contract: At least 50 bytes with the first byte being 0x00 (NUL). The NUL byte at position 0 causes strlen to return 0 after fgets reads the data, making end == line and triggering the underflow at *(end - 1) = 0.
